sections.content:
Population change in Kensington and Chelsea in 2032

The population in Kensington and Chelsea is projected to increase from 146,392 people in 2022 to 159,403 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net international migration, which will increase the population by 29,077 people.

This is different to the majority of areas in England, where net internal migration is projected to be the biggest factor in population change.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Kensington and Chelsea
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Kensington and Chelsea, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More births than deaths mean that the population is projected to increase by 6,250, with 15,561 births and 9,311 deaths in Kensington and Chelsea between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would increase the population in Kensington and Chelsea by 4.3%, compared with an increase of 6.0% in London and an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to reduce the population by 23,154, with 146,134 people moving to the area and 169,288 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Kensington and Chelsea by 15.8%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to increase the population by 648, with 4,124 people moving to the area and 3,476 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Kensington and Chelsea by 0.4%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 29,077, with 70,241 people moving to the area and 41,164 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Kensington and Chelsea by 19.9%, compared with an increase of 14.7% in London and an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Kensington and Chelsea in 2032

The median age in Kensington and Chelsea is projected to fall from 38 years in 2022 to 37 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 16% of the population in Kensington and Chelsea are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 14% in 2022.

sections.title: The 50 to 59 age group are set to see the largest change in Kensington and Chelsea between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Kensington and Chelsea is projected to stay the same, at around 71%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 188 to 205 over the same time period.

This is below average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Kensington and Chelsea?

In 2032, 15% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 17% in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Kensington and Chelsea between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will rise from 4% to 5%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 6% to 5%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will fall from 6% to 5%
